items.title: Cosey Fanni Tutti at 75: the art of refusing to conform
items.summary: Cosey Fanni Tutti, co-founder of Throbbing Gristle, turned 75 on 4 November 2026. A look at her five-decade career in music, performance and writing.
items.fullText:
Happy 75th birthday to Cosey Fanni Tutti – musician, performance artist, writer, co-founder of Throbbing Gristle and one of the most uncompromising creative figures in the history of industrial music.

Born on November 4, 1951, in Hull, England, Cosey Fanni Tutti has spent more than five decades challenging the boundaries between music, performance, sexuality, identity and artistic freedom. Her career is a remarkable demonstration of what happens when an artist refuses to separate personal experience from creative expression.

Her earliest experiments with COUM Transmissions, beginning in 1969, confronted audiences with ideas that conventional artistic institutions were often reluctant to accommodate. By treating her own body, experiences and work within the sex industry as artistic material, Cosey questioned the mechanisms through which women were represented, consumed and judged. The resulting performances and exhibitions were provocative, certainly, but their impact extended well beyond shock value. They demanded that audiences reconsider who controls an image, who assigns its meaning and who has the authority to define art.

From COUM Transmissions to Throbbing Gristle

In 1976, alongside Chris Carter, Genesis P-Orridge and Peter Christopherson, she established Throbbing Gristle, the collective that would fundamentally alter the vocabulary of experimental electronic music. That October, COUM Transmissions’ notorious “Prostitution” exhibition at London’s Institute of Contemporary Arts, accompanied by a performance by Throbbing Gristle on October 18, provoked outrage in the British press and Parliament. Conservative MP Nicholas Fairbairn famously denounced the artists as “wreckers of civilisation.”

Fifty years later, the phrase sounds rather more like an accidental compliment.

Throbbing Gristle’s confrontation with established musical structures helped create the foundations of industrial music. Cosey’s guitar, cornet, voice and unconventional approach to performance were integral to a sound that rejected the comfortable distinction between musical expression and disturbing experience.

But reducing her achievements to Throbbing Gristle would overlook much of her artistic journey.

About Cosey Fanni Tutti

Following the group’s original dissolution in 1981, her partnership with Chris Carter developed into Chris & Cosey, later Carter Tutti, producing an extraordinary catalogue of electronic music that explored rhythm, sensuality, atmosphere and experimentation. Their subsequent collaboration with Nik Colk Void as Carter Tutti Void brought those instincts into a more improvisational, rhythmically driven setting.

Her solo work tells another key part of the story. From “Time to Tell” (1983) through “TUTTI” (2019) and “Delia Derbyshire: The Myths and the Legendary Tapes” (2022) to 2025’s “2t2,” Cosey has continued developing her own sonic language, moving between tactile electronic rhythms, intimate reflection and expansive experimentation.

Her writing carries equal weight. “Art Sex Music” (2017) offered a candid account of her life and artistic development, while “Re-Sisters” (2022) examined connections between her own experiences and those of electronic pioneer Delia Derbyshire and medieval mystic Margery Kempe. Across radically different historical circumstances, the book explores the determination of women to pursue their own identities despite considerable resistance.

The timing of her 75th birthday is especially meaningful. On October 18, 2026, the Institute of Contemporary Arts commemorated the 50th anniversary of Throbbing Gristle’s historic appearance at the venue, returning attention to one of the defining moments in the development of industrial culture.

Meanwhile, “Art Sex Music,” a feature documentary directed by Caroline Catz and based on Cosey’s 2017 memoir, has completed filming and entered post-production. On December 4, Mute is scheduled to release “TG24+,” an extensive limited-edition archival collection featuring 36 Throbbing Gristle live performances, newly restored and mastered by Chris Carter.

Yet Cosey Fanni Tutti’s work reaches far beyond her historical influence. Her 2025 album “2t2” is a reminder that her creative life remains active, inquisitive and intensely personal.

Perhaps her greatest achievement is that she has never allowed the past to become a comfortable artistic identity. She has continued questioning the assumptions of the very culture she helped transform, refusing to become merely a monument to industrial music’s revolutionary beginnings.

At 75, Cosey Fanni Tutti remains an extraordinary example of artistic independence: a woman who has consistently insisted on defining herself, her work and her relationship with the world on her own terms.

Happy birthday, Cosey. Thank you for the music, the courage, the intelligence and more than five decades of refusing to be conveniently categorised.

Some artists follow the evolution of culture. Others change the conditions under which culture is created. Cosey Fanni Tutti belongs firmly among the latter.

items.title: Telex share new version of ‘Twist A Saint-Tropez’ from ‘MAXI’
items.summary: Belgian synthpop pioneers Telex shared a new Maxi Version of their 1978 debut single "Twist A Saint-Tropez," taken from the album "MAXI," out 4 December 2026.
items.fullText:
Belgian synthpop pioneers Telex shared a new Maxi Version of “Twist A Saint-Tropez,” their 1978 debut single, on 3 November 2026. The track is taken from “MAXI,” an album of 13 extended mixes due on double vinyl and CD on 4 December 2026 via Mute.

“Twist A Saint-Tropez” was Telex’s cover of Les Chats Sauvages’ 1960s hit, and its original 1978 release launched the Brussels trio into wider recognition. For “MAXI,” surviving members Dan Lacksman and Michel Moers revisited the original tapes to build new extended versions, remastered and remixed while keeping the catalog’s original character.

“MAXI” also includes extended versions of “Euro-vision,” Telex’s 1980 Eurovision Song Contest entry for Belgium, and the band’s deadpan cover of Bill Haley’s “Rock Around The Clock,” which led to a 1979 Top of the Pops appearance. The album is released on double transparent red and blue vinyl and CD on 4 December 2026, with a digital edition to follow in 2027.

About Telex

Telex is a Belgian synthpop trio formed in Brussels in 1978 by Marc Moulin, Dan Lacksman and Michel Moers, among the first acts to bring electronic pop to the mainstream. The band released albums through 2006 before announcing its retirement in 2008 following Moulin’s death in the same year.

In 2021, the surviving members began a new partnership with Mute, starting with the compilation “This Is Telex,” featuring unreleased tracks alongside newly mixed and remastered catalog reissues. Telex also released a box set collecting the band’s six studio albums, and Michel Moers issued the solo single “Microwaves,” featuring Claudia Brücken of Propaganda, in 2024. “MAXI,” arriving 4 December 2026, extends that reissue campaign with new extended versions of the band’s catalog.

items.title: Magnetic Skies signs with Over The Border Records
items.summary: UK synthpop and darkwave band Magnetic Skies has signed with Over The Border Records' booking division, ahead of a third album due November 2027.
items.fullText:
UK synthpop and darkwave band Magnetic Skies has signed with Over The Border Records‘ booking division. The label announced the signing on 3 November 2026.

Magnetic Skies is a synthpop and darkwave project formed by vocalist and keyboardist Simon Kent and keyboardist Jo Womar, built around vintage analogue textures and cinematic modern songwriting. The band released its latest album, “Fragments”, in November 2025 via ReprinT.

The band said: “We’ve always wanted to take Magnetic Skies beyond the UK and build a connection with audiences across Europe, so we’re really excited to be working with Davide and Over The Border Records. Germany is a particularly interesting territory for us, and with our third album coming in November 2027, it feels like the right time to start making those connections. We’re looking forward to working together, playing some great shows and introducing Magnetic Skies to new audiences.”

Davide Pulito, CEO of Over The Border Records, added: “I’m excited to announce the signing of Magnetic Skies. I loved their sound from the very first moment so I can’t wait to book gigs for the next album promotion. Welcome on board guys!”

Magnetic Skies’ next confirmed date is 3 December 2026 at The Grace in London.

About Magnetic Skies

Magnetic Skies is a London-based synthpop and darkwave band whose lineup includes Simon Kent on vocals, keyboards, guitar and bass, Jo Womar on keyboards and vocals, and Lenin Alegria on drums. The project launched with the single “Suffocate” in June 2023, followed by the debut album “Empire Falling” that November.

The band returned in July 2025 with the single “Back To Life,” then announced its second album, “Fragments”, alongside the single “Everything’s Alright” and a run of UK headline dates. “Fragments” was released via ReprinT on 7 November 2025. With the Over The Border Records signing, Magnetic Skies is now building toward its third album, planned for November 2027.

items.title: Breathing Records releases compilation ‘Inhale Vol. II’
items.summary: Breathing Records released the compilation "Inhale Vol. II" on 30 October 2026, with 11 tracks from 13 artists including Unter Strøm, Zaatar and Sleek Teeth.
items.fullText:
Breathing Records released the compilation “Inhale Vol. II” on 30 October 2026. The album gathers 11 previously unreleased tracks from 13 artists, with cover artwork by Jesse Draxler.

“Inhale” is Breathing Records’ recurring discovery and collaboration project. Each volume follows a shared conceptual thread and spans multiple genres. “Inhale Vol. II” follows “Inhale Vol. I,” released in November 2025, and continues the label’s pairing of established and emerging acts from across industrial, darkwave and electronic subgenres.

The tracklist includes Houses of Heaven’s “Liaison,” Lavion’s “Millennial Dust,” The New Division’s “Pleasure to Yourself,” Half Joy’s “Killing the Fear,” Unter Strøm‘s “Ghost in Wires,” a Pixel Grip and MVTANT collaboration remixing “Club Mania (Snap Yo Neck),” Local Suicide and Skelesys’ “Heartbeat,” Sleek Teeth‘s “Disengage,” Zaatar‘s “Bahnsteigkante,” Void Palace’s “Set Me Free” and Snakes of Russia’s “Axe to Grind.”

“Inhale Vol. II” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp, Spotify and Apple Music.

About Breathing Records

Breathing Records is an independent label based in San Diego, California, founded in 2025 in service of avant-garde, underground, industrial and dark electronic music. The label’s “Inhale” compilation series is its core discovery and collaboration project. It brings together artists across genres and subcultures under a shared conceptual thread.

The label’s roster includes Unter Strøm, whose Breathing Records releases span the “Fragment” and “Fold” singles, the album “Between Forms,” its closing single “Stumbling,” and the live recording “Transmission 003: Live at the Breathing Records Showcase.” Zaatar released the single “Bahnsteigkante” on the label in October 2026, the same track that appears on “Inhale Vol. II.” “Inhale Vol. I,” the series’ first volume, arrived in November 2025 with contributions from Street Fever and Matte Blvck, among others.

items.title: Apoptygma Berzerk shares 1994 ‘Who Am I?’ remix of Sabotage on YouTube
items.summary: Apoptygma Berzerk uploaded their 1994 remix of Sabotage Qu'est-ce Que C'est's "Who Am I?" to YouTube on 4 November 2026, from the CD "Annorlunda."
items.fullText:
Apoptygma Berzerk uploaded their remix of “Who Am I?” by German electro-industrial act Sabotage Qu’est-ce Que C’est to their official YouTube channel on 4 November 2026. The track dates back 32 years, to a period when Apoptygma Berzerk were beginning to reach audiences beyond Norway.

Originally released on the six-track CD “Annorlunda” in 1994, the remix was produced and arranged by Apoptygma Berzerk, with Per Aksel Lundgreen credited as release coordinator.

The connection between Apoptygma Berzerk and Sabotage was not limited to a remix. On 10 April 1994, Apoptygma Berzerk played their first concert in Germany, at the Indie Market mini-festival at Kaue in Gelsenkirchen. Also on the bill that evening were Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? and Steril.

Per Aksel Lundgreen, who was part of Apoptygma Berzerk during those early years, recalled the concert in a later interview with Belgian music website Snoozecontrol. The band also marked the anniversary on Facebook in April 2020, noting that the same day brought their first television interview, for Off Beat TV.

A further connection runs through the two acts: Sabotage vocalist Isabelle Gernand was involved in Angst Pop’s “Viva Ta Vie,” remixed by Stephan Groth and released on “Electronic Youth – Vol. 3” in 1995, with songwriting credits shared by Gernand, Groth and Lundgreen.

The remix has circulated online before, but its upload to Apoptygma Berzerk’s official channel marks the first time it has appeared there.

About Apoptygma Berzerk

Apoptygma Berzerk is a Norwegian electronic act formed in Sarpsborg in 1989 by Stephan Groth and Jon Erik Martinsen. The band’s first German concert, on 10 April 1994 at the Indie Market mini-festival in Gelsenkirchen, placed them alongside German act Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? and Steril; Germany went on to become one of Apoptygma Berzerk’s most important markets, with a large and consistent fan base through later decades. The band remixed Sabotage’s “Who Am I?” the same year, released on the CD “Annorlunda.”

Apoptygma Berzerk has continued to revisit its back catalogue. A 25th-anniversary feature on the band’s hit “Kathy’s Song” detailed the song’s Ferry Corsten remix history, and the band’s 2022 “Black Pawn” compilation continued an ongoing rarities series. The 1994 “Who Am I?” remix, now on the band’s official YouTube channel, extends that same archival thread back to the project’s earliest years abroad.

Sabotage, the act credited on the original “Who Am I?,” has had its own more recent Side-Line coverage: the project’s four-track EP “No Bottom – No Top” is set for release on EMMO.BIZ Records in January 2027, reworking earlier Sabotage tracks including “Souvenir” and “Ewigkeit.”

items.title: Spammerheads and Azote Mental announce split LP ‘Resistencia al Impacto’
items.summary: Spanish EBM act Spammerheads and Madrid synthpunk-EBM project Azote Mental release the split LP "Resistencia al Impacto" on Caustic Records, 10 December 2026.
items.fullText:
Spanish EBM act Spammerheads and Madrid-based synthpunk-EBM project Azote Mental will release a split LP, “Resistencia al Impacto,” on Caustic Records on 10 December 2026. The album is available for pre-order as a splatter-colored 12″ vinyl, limited to 300 copies.

The split pairs four new EBM tracks from Spammerheads, based in Valencia, with five tracks from Azote Mental, including the live favorites “Deseo” and “Vidas Heladas” alongside previously unreleased material. Caustic Records describes Spammerheads as one of Spain’s leading EBM acts and Azote Mental’s inclusion as the band’s first-ever vinyl pressing.

“Resistencia al Impacto” is available to pre-order on Bandcamp ahead of its 10 December 2026 release.

About Spammerheads

Spammerheads is an EBM act based in Valencia, Spain. The band has released music through Caustic Records, including a 2022 vinyl EP. In 2025, Spammerheads collaborated with Nightcrawler on the single “Ghostless” and released the album “The Mire Chronicles,” a record informed by the 2024 Valencia floods. “Resistencia al Impacto,” the band’s split LP with Azote Mental, follows in December 2026 with four new tracks.

About Azote Mental

Azote Mental is a synthpunk-EBM project based in Madrid, Spain. “Resistencia al Impacto” marks the band’s first release pressed to vinyl, featuring the live tracks “Deseo” and “Vidas Heladas” alongside previously unreleased material, released through Caustic Records alongside Valencia act Spammerheads.

items.title: X Marks The Pedwalk’s ‘Freaks’ returns on coloured vinyl
items.summary: X Marks The Pedwalk's 1992 debut album "Freaks" returns as a limited coloured vinyl LP in the Zoth Ommog Classix reissue series, with new cover art.
items.fullText:
X Marks The Pedwalk‘s 1992 debut album “Freaks” has been reissued as a strictly limited 12″ coloured vinyl LP, with new cover artwork, as the second release in the Zoth Ommog Classix reissue series.

“Freaks” was the German industrial duo’s first full-length release, produced by Sevren Ni-arb and AL/X/S and preceded by the “Abattoir” single. The album carries the tracks “Abattoir,” “Zest,” “Repression,” “Swastika,” “Express My Sentiments Exactly,” “The Shot,” “Helpless,” “Battered Babies,” “Church for Snow White” and “Epilogue: Desert in Dawn.” It was originally released by Zoth Ommog in Europe and later issued in North America by Metropolis Records with different artwork and a longer tracklist.

About X Marks The Pedwalk

X Marks The Pedwalk is a German industrial project led by Sevren Ni-arb (André Schmechta), formed in Münster. “Freaks,” released through Zoth Ommog in 1992, was the project’s debut full-length album, recorded with original member Regan Eracs, who left after the follow-up single “Cenotaph.” The band went on to release further albums on Zoth Ommog and later Metropolis Records, including “Human Desolation,” “The Killing Had Begun,” “Meshwork,” “Drawback” and “Inner Zone Journey.”

X Marks The Pedwalk, now fronted by Sevren Ni-arb alongside vocalist Estefanía, has continued releasing music on meshwork music, including the 2022 album “New/End,” 2023’s “Superstition” and 2025’s “Insomnia,” most recently previewed by the singles “Light Your Mind” and “Bury Me.”

The “Freaks” reissue is the second entry in the Zoth Ommog Classix vinyl series, which began in September 2026 with Lights Of Euphoria’s ‘Brainstorm’ reissue.

items.title: EISGRAU releases debut single ‘Rabengesang’
items.summary: German dark rock project EISGRAU released its debut single "Rabengesang" on 1 November 2026, self-released out of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
items.fullText:
German dark rock project EISGRAU released its debut single, “Rabengesang”, on 1 November 2026. The self-released track comes out of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania in northeastern Germany and is available as a digital single on Spotify.

EISGRAU combines cold, driving drum rhythms with dark synthesizer textures, electric guitar riffs and reverb-heavy vocals, drawing on the Baltic Sea coast and the misty forests of the region. “Rabengesang” deals with transience, inner shadows and human longing, casting the raven as a silent observer from the darkness.

About EISGRAU

EISGRAU is a solo dark rock project based in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Germany. “Rabengesang,” released on 1 November 2026, is the project’s debut single, issued independently without a label. The track was promoted to DJs and the dark music scene through the DarkTraxx mailing service.

items.title: Crá Croí releases debut album ‘Tá brón orm’
items.summary: Cork duo Crá Croí has released its self-produced debut album "Tá brón orm," an 11-track record preceded by three advance singles.
items.fullText:
Cork, Ireland duo Crá Croí has released its debut album, “Tá brón orm” (Irish for “sadness is on me”), on 30 October 2026. The self-produced, self-released record fuses post-punk atmospheres with synth-driven beats and cinematic production across eleven tracks, following eight standalone singles the duo has released since November 2025, three of them pulled from the album itself.

Crá Croí is RG and CD. RG writes, plays, produces, mixes and masters the material; CD provides vocals and painted the album’s cover artwork, and also co-produced the record. The logo is by Marc O’Grady and the crow artwork by David O’Donovan. Crá Croí describes “Tá brón orm” as “an ambitious and deeply philosophical journey” whose lyrics explore “the bleak realities of war and nuclear devastation,” drawing on 1980s apocalyptic cinema and weaving existential questions together with themes from Irish mythology.

“Tá brón orm” runs eleven tracks: “On The Fringes,” “Lord Of The Wild,” “Black Snow,” “Just Another Day,” “Sirens,” “Threads,” “Croí,” “Whispers In The Sea,” “Swords Into Ploughshares,” “Ghosts In The Bog” and “When The Wind Blows.” The album is available as a digital download on Bandcamp.

Three singles preceded ‘Tá brón orm’

Three songs from the album arrived as advance singles ahead of the October release. “Lord Of The Wild”, released 7 August 2026 and covered by Side-Line at the time, draws on the Irish myth of Cernunnos, the horned figure tied to sacred groves and ancient places. “Black Snow” followed on 4 September 2026. “Just Another Day”, issued 2 October 2026 as the album’s third and final pre-release single, puts modern life’s emotions down to performance, with authenticity swapped for what the duo call “superficial substitutes.”

About Crá Croí

Crá Croí is a duo based in Cork, Ireland, working under the initials RG and CD. RG writes, plays, produces, mixes and masters the group’s material; CD provides vocals and handles the project’s artwork and visuals, including the self-made videos that accompany each single. The duo released its debut single, “Radiation Romance,” on 10 November 2025, pairing a nuclear-annihilation theme with a motorik groove. Four more standalone singles followed: “Fires At Dawn” in December 2025, “Feeding The Fear” in January 2026, “Lost In The Electric Blood” in March 2026, and “Flesh Machines” later in the year.

From August 2026, Crá Croí drew its next three singles directly from its forthcoming album. Side-Line covered “Lord Of The Wild” in July 2026 ahead of its August release, and “Just Another Day” in September 2026 ahead of its October release. “Tá brón orm,” Crá Croí’s first full-length release, followed on 30 October 2026 with eleven tracks.

items.title: LMBW – Architecture Of Collapse (Digital Album – Ant-zen)
items.summary: French artist Cyril Laurent has been active in the music world for over 30 years,...
items.fullText:
French artist Cyril Laurent has been active in the music world for over 30 years, having made a name for himself through his project Lambwool. With LMBW, he set out to explore the more Electronic side of his musical vision. Two years ago, he released the EP “Crossed Parallels”—an absolute masterpiece—and now follows it up with this eight-track album, conceived as the musical expression of a mind in turmoil.

LMBW continues along the path established on the EP, delivering highly intelligent compositions in which every track is meticulously constructed. The music resembles a sonic puzzle, with every piece fitting perfectly into the next. This is the work of a true sound architect: an artist who takes the time to craft individual sounds before seamlessly combining them with a variety of effects and rhythms. At the same time, the album carries strong Cinematic influences, thanks to its distinctive atmosphere, which leaves plenty of room for the imagination.

The album brings to mind a surgical approach to composition, with everything crafted with extraordinary precision and attention to detail. An absolute masterpiece! (Rating:9).

Listen to “Eructating”:

About LBWL

LBWL is an alias of French musician Cyril Laurent, who has recorded since 2000 under the name Lambwool. Laurent started in the early 1990s in the Marseille metal band Moon Revolution and released the 1996 EP “French Kissin” as The Soul Lives in Berlin. Lambwool’s ambient and cinematic work cites Dead Can Dance, Tangerine Dream, Labradford, Brian Eno, and The Young Gods among its influences.

The Lambwool discography includes “Fading Landscapes” in 2005 and “…And The Angel Is Gone” in 2008 on Divine Comedy Records, “Mono” in 2009, “A Sky Through The Wall” in 2012, the Nicolas Dick collaboration “Post” in 2014, and “Vanish” in 2014 on OPN, the self-released albums “Islandi” in 2018 and “Isolation” in 2020, and “Ashes” in 2025 on Cyclic Law. Laurent introduced the LBWL alias with the 2024 mini-album “Crossed Parallels” on Ant-Zen, followed by the project’s first full album, “Architecture Of Collapse,” released on the same label on June 9, 2026.

items.title: Machine Command release ‘Uncontrolable’ ahead of 2027 album
items.summary: Rotterdam EBM duo Machine Command released "Uncontrolable" on 2 November 2026, a two-track single previewing an untitled album due spring 2027.
items.fullText:
Rotterdam EBM duo Machine Command released “Uncontrolable” on 2 November 2026, a two-track digital single that precedes an as yet untitled album scheduled for spring 2027.

Annemarie Janssen wrote the lyrics and Pieter Winkelaar the music. The duo describes the title track as a piece about machine intelligence turning on its makers: “It’s about conceited self-assured and self learning beings who threaten to wipe out humanity.”

The B-side is a remix of the album track “Predators” by The Peoples Republic Of Europe. The source track runs at 165 BPM, and the remixer moved it out of EBM tempo entirely. Machine Command stated that The Peoples Republic Of Europe “transformed the fast paced EBM to Drum& bass!”

“Uncontrolable” runs 4:30 and the “Predators” remix 3:50. Both tracks are available as a digital single on Bandcamp. The cover photo is credited to Ionut and the artwork design to Design Tiger Design.

About Machine Command

Machine Command formed in 2013 in Rotterdam, The Netherlands, as a duo playing EBM. The project lists KRAT on electronics and JAANSEN on vocals.

The duo has built a long run of self-released digital titles through Bandcamp, among them “Tetrarchy E.P.”, “To The Point”, “Without Fear EP”, “New Socialism”, “Not Doing It”, “Stampfbereit”, “Without Fear V2.0”, “Two Point Zero”, “Die Rote Linie”, “Decline and Rise Again”, “Nuke It from Orbit”, “Cathected” and “Rage”. Side-Line covered the band in November 2024 when they issued the Machine Command present EBM infested ‘Affected’ album, the release that preceded the current run of singles.

The remixer on the new B-side has his own history in Side-Line’s pages. The Peoples Republic Of Europe appeared on the site in August 2013 with the New ‘Feel The Power’ album by The Peoples Republic Of Europe out now item.

“Uncontrolable” is the second single the duo has drawn from those album sessions.

items.title: Liars share ‘Beat Creep Some Eyes’ video
items.summary: Liars released a video for "Beat Creep Some Eyes", from their album "A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans", out 5 March 2027 on Mute, and set a London date.
items.fullText:
Liars released a video for “Beat Creep Some Eyes”, the latest track from their forthcoming eleventh studio album, “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans”, due 5 March 2027 on Mute.

The video was shot by visual collaborator Clemens Habicht on an obsolete 3D camera in and around Kalamazoo, Michigan, the city that inspired the album, after Angus Andrew relocated there with his family. Discussing the track, Andrew said: “Sometimes I think the strangest thing isn’t that the world is absurd, but how quickly we get used to it. You can find yourself living inside something completely ridiculous and, after a while, it just becomes Tuesday.”

Liars announced “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans” in September; “Beat Creep Some Eyes” follows lead track “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo” as the second piece of music shared from the record. The album was written and recorded between the United States and Australia, where Andrew now lives, with Laurence Pike and Cameron Deyell, both collaborators on 2021’s “The Apple Drop”.

Liars also confirmed a London show at Village Underground on 15 May 2027, with tickets on sale from 10am on 6 November. The band play Drum’s Not Dead 20th-anniversary shows at Phoenix Central Park in Sydney on 26 and 27 November 2026.

“A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans” tracklist: “Happy Or Not”, “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo”, “Laced Plume”, “Urgent As Always”, “Deep Deeper”, “Disaster Tropes”, “Beat Creep Some Eyes”, “Real Time Trespasser”, “SHAME!”, “Retention Arc”, “Out Of Order”.

The album will be released on vinyl, CD and digitally through Mute.

About Liars

Liars formed in New York in 2000 around Angus Andrew. The band’s catalogue spans “They Threw Us All In A Trench And Stuck A Monument On Top” (2001), “Drums Not Dead” (2006), “TFCF” (2017) and “The Apple Drop” (2021). After “The Apple Drop”, Andrew paused making music to found the record label No Gold, before relocating to Kalamazoo, Michigan, an experience that shaped “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans”. The album reunites Andrew with “The Apple Drop” collaborators Laurence Pike and Cameron Deyell, and is set for release on 5 March 2027 through Mute, preceded by the singles “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo” and “Beat Creep Some Eyes”.

German electro act Accessory opened pre-orders on 4 November for “Outrun The End”, a nine-track vinyl collection due 27 November 2026 through Infacted Recordings, pressed in a limited edition of 200 copies worldwide.

“Outrun The End” draws nine tracks from Accessory’s catalogue, including “Dark Gothic Queen,” “Outrun the Gun,” “Deadline” and “No Man Covers.” The B-side opens with Feindflug’s remix of “War of Emotions.”

Tracklist:

Side B: “War of Emotions” (Feindflug remix), “What The Hell,” “Bad Conditions,” “Lifesaver”

About Accessory

Accessory’s history goes back to 1994, when Dirk Steyer and Kay Resch started the project in Chemnitz, Germany, under the name Voices of Darkness. Two years later, they renamed the project Accessory. Over the following decades, the duo released albums including “Jukka2147.de” (2001), “Titan” (2003), “More Than Machinery” (2008) and “Elektrik” (2019), sharing stages with acts such as And One and Hocico. “Outrun The End” brings together nine tracks spanning that catalogue on a limited vinyl pressing through Infacted Recordings.

items.title: Seances share video for Assemblage 23’s remix of debut single ‘Fade’
items.summary: Milwaukee post-punk band Seances release a video for "Fade (Assemblage 23 Rmx)", Tom Shear's remix of their debut single, directed by Kyle Arpke.
items.fullText:
Milwaukee post-punk band Seances have released a video for “Fade (Assemblage 23 Rmx)”, Tom Shear’s remix of their debut single “Fade”, retitled “Killing Karma” for the clip. The remix came out on Bandcamp on 31 October 2026; the video, directed and edited by Kyle Lloyd Arpke with artwork by Ashley Altadonna of Tall Lady Productions, follows now.

Seances is the project of Eric Arsnow (vocals, bass, guitar, drums, programming) and guitarist Jason Kartz, who helped develop “Fade” from Arsnow’s initial sketches; Dexter and Paxton Arsnow contribute backing vocals. Arsnow formed Seances after seeing The Chameleons play in Milwaukee in 2023, and cites The Cure and Joy Division as influences alongside the Metropolis, Wax Trax! and Cleopatra label compilations. Shear’s remix, as Assemblage 23, adds an electronic layer to the band’s post-punk arrangement of “Fade”.

Arsnow described working with Shear on the remix: “Being able to work with Assemblage 23 on this remix of Fade was a dream come true.”

“Fade” first appeared on Seances’ debut album “Power Is A Phantom”. The band’s live line-up draws on members with ties to The Promise Ring, Masked Intruder, Tigernite, Fight Dice and BvsMV, and a second album, “Silent Salvation”, is planned for 2027. On 23 October 2026 the band released “Tame”, a name-your-price Bandcamp track dedicated to Arsnow’s late friend Francisco Ramirez, with proceeds passed to a fundraiser for Ramirez’s daughter.

About Seances

Seances are a post-punk band from Milwaukee, Wisconsin, formed by Eric Arsnow after seeing The Chameleons perform in the city in 2023. Arsnow writes and records as the project’s core member, playing vocals, bass, guitar, drums and programming, with guitarist Jason Kartz contributing to arrangements including “Fade”, and Dexter and Paxton Arsnow on backing vocals. The band’s sound draws on The Cure and Joy Division, filtered through the Metropolis, Wax Trax! and Cleopatra label compilations Arsnow grew up listening to. Seances released their debut single “Weighted” in January 2025 ahead of their debut album “Power Is A Phantom”, which includes “Fade”. A second album, “Silent Salvation”, is due in 2027. The band’s live members have previously played with The Promise Ring, Masked Intruder, Tigernite, Fight Dice and BvsMV. The “Fade (Assemblage 23 Rmx)” video, released under the title “Killing Karma”, marks the band’s first collaboration with Tom Shear’s long-running electro-industrial project Assemblage 23.

items.fullText:
Masterful reinterpretation – Thessla covers "The Things You Said"

As a loy­al Depeche Mode fan and lov­er of soph­ist­ic­ated cov­er ver­sions, I always approach rein­ter­pret­a­tions with great scep­ti­cism. Simply play­ing along isn’t enough to make an impres­sion on me.

However, this new ver­sion of this won­der­ful bal­lad from 1987 proves that there is anoth­er way. Brilliantly reima­gined, Thessla, in col­lab­or­a­tion with the sing­er MQNQ, suc­ceeds here in cre­at­ing a fas­cin­at­ing son­ic aes­thet­ic that lends synth pop an unex­pec­ted depth. The atmo­spher­ic rich­ness cap­tures the mel­an­chol­ic spir­it of the ori­gin­al and con­fid­ently brings it into the present day. On my web­site, The (Al)Most Complete Depeche Mode Covers & Tributes Archive, this suc­cess­ful track will, of course, take its right­ful place in the next update.

items.title: Milano Flash – Bits And Pieces
items.summary: Milano Flash enchants with “Bits And Pieces” through its innocent youthful charm and subtle 80s Italo-disco sounds.
items.fullText:
Electro pop with 80s charm

Right from the very first listen, Milano Flash’s ‘Bits And Pieces’ exudes a won­der­ful, inno­cent and youth­ful charm. Whilst this elec­tro-pop track from Greece may not spark a music­al revolu­tion, it pos­sesses pre­cisely the subtle qual­it­ies needed to strike a genu­ine chord. In its son­ic DNA, I’m imme­di­ately drawn in by a dis­tinct hint of 1980s Italo-disco, which lends the mel­an­chol­ic under­tone an unex­pec­tedly driv­ing, time­less lightness.

Anyone expect­ing an over­pro­duced, heavy-handed track will be sur­prised. Instead, the song car­ries an unpre­ten­tious, intim­ate aura that touches you dir­ectly and lingers in the memory.

items.summary: Nightsisters’ ‘All Things Must End’ combines icy cold wave, deep baritone vocals and driving beats to create a dense, gripping sound.

Right from the start, Nightsisters’ ‘All Things Must End’ exerts a power­ful pull. A juicy beat and a punchy bass drive the intro for­ward, whilst the dense, frosty cold wave sound cre­ates an intensely sombre atmosphere.
